title: Unsynchronized Type-Safe Memory Slab Access
pattern: Accessing an object allocated from a type-safe memory slab (e.g. `SLAB_TYPESAFE_BY_RCU`) under RCU protection without re-verifying the object's key.
why_bad: Type-safe memory guarantees that the slab memory will not be returned to the OS (preventing page faults), but it allows the object to be freed and re-allocated as a *new* object of the same type. Failing to re-verify the object's identity/key means acting on the wrong data.
detection: RCU reader accessing a type-safe slab-allocated node without comparing its stored key/ID against the requested search key under lock.
counterexample: Acquiring the per-element lock and verifying the key matches before acting.
